A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same EpiRC-PGS research. Their main text, figures, algorithms, equations, and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including matching reorganized proof sections.

before.justification: v3 reports original simulations comparing EpiRC-PGS with Lagrangian methods across three RCMDP/CMDP settings, averaged over ten random seeds (Section 6, Figure 3).

after.justification: v4 retains the original simulations and comparative results in Section 6 and Figure 3.

M1.justification: The epigraph formulation, bisection search, projected policy-gradient subroutine, and finite/KL uncertainty evaluators retain their procedures. Algorithm 2 already selects the best evaluated iterate in both versions.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same randomly generated tabular settings: RCMDP with five transition kernels, RCMDP with KL uncertainty, and singleton-uncertainty CMDP (Section 6).

E2.justification: Figure 3 retains LF and LF-π(k)-avg in all three settings, with occupancy-averaged LF and the LP optimum additionally included in the CMDP comparison.

E3.justification: Section 6 and Appendix D retain environment sampling, state/action sizes, discounts, five constraints, learning rates, and evaluation metrics. Inner-loop budgets remain 10,000 iterations for settings (a, c) and 1,000 for (b).

E4.justification: The gradient-conflict example and landscape illustration in Figure 1, together with Figure 3's feasibility and convergence analyses, are retained. No ablation, sensitivity study, or additional robustness analysis is introduced.

E5.justification: Both versions report averaging Figure 3 results over ten random seeds. Repeated-run information and uncertainty-reporting practices are unchanged.

E6.justification: The plotted results and numerical annotations in Figures 1–3 are unchanged. Section 6 retains the same feasibility findings and performance comparisons; no experimental result entries are added or removed.

T1.justification: Section 2.2 corrects the return definition from summing μ(s)V(s) over state-action pairs to summing over states, removing an erroneous extra action summation. The substantive theorem statements, assumptions, rates, and proof arguments are retained.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the gradient-conflict finding, epigraph-based solution, and claimed first near-optimal RCMDP policy-identification guarantee with approximately O(ε^-4) robust policy evaluations.

C2.justification: v3's Remark 3, titled 'Last-iterate convergence' and invoking Corollary 1, becomes v4's Remark 2 on 'Best-iterate convergence' under Theorem 5. This clarifies the guarantee associated with the unchanged selection rule. Section 7's limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendices C–D retain evaluator pseudocode, implementation settings, and the source-code link. The uniform initial distribution newly stated in Example 1 was already specified in v3's Appendix H, now Appendix G.

R1.justification: The bibliography and substantive research positioning are retained. Appendix A.1 removes a redundant sentence contrasting prior epigraph studies with the proposed robustness treatment, but preserves that contrast in the following passage.

P1.justification: v4 makes localized wording and notation edits, adds a contents page, and consolidates appendix sections. The MDP lemmas join Appendix F, and the formerly separate proof appendices I and J become Appendix H; the main narrative remains intact.

P2.justification: v4 adds the contents-page layout and adjusts appendix spacing and algorithm placement. Figure 1(a)'s caption changes δ > 0 to δ ≥ 0. Table 1 and the plotted graphics remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: v4 improves mathematical and explanatory precision by correcting the return definition and replacing the misleading last-iterate characterization with a best-iterate statement consistent with Algorithm 2. The contents page and consolidated appendices improve navigation. These are limited gains; the method and experimental evidence remain unchanged.
